title: Use semantic design-token roles
examples: accent, surface, textPrimary instead of component-local color literals
anti_patterns: hard-coded ALINA palette inside shared UI components
tests: shared primitive contains no theme-specific raw color

title: Shared UI primitives remain theme-agnostic
examples: GlassPanel consumes surface/border/glow tokens
anti_patterns: importing ALINA app theme constants into packages/ui
tests: packages/ui does not depend on apps/alina-control-center

title: Motion requires reduced-motion fallback
examples: disable decorative parallax when prefers-reduced-motion is active
anti_patterns: cinematic motion with no non-animated path
tests: reduced-motion mode remains fully usable

title: Interactive controls expose visible keyboard focus
examples: focus-visible ring uses semantic focus token
anti_patterns: mouse-only affordance
tests: tab navigation shows visible focus for every interactive primitive

title: Primary stream owns visual attention
examples: active task is primary; background indexing is visually suppressed
anti_patterns: all events rendered with equal urgency
tests: background activity cannot visually overpower primary task

title: Avatar identity is independent from presentation mode
examples: ALINA can switch from full-body hologram to compact assistant without losing state
anti_patterns: avatar business state embedded inside one 3D scene
tests: avatar state survives presentation-mode switch

title: Workspace presentation state is separate from domain data
examples: panel focus/collapse/dock state can change without mutating document/task data
anti_patterns: storing domain payload inside layout nodes
tests: workspace transitions do not modify panel domain payload references

title: Workspace layout state must be serializable
examples: JSON-safe layout with panel IDs, regions, order, focus and collapsed state
anti_patterns: React elements/functions stored directly in persisted workspace state
tests: JSON.stringify/parse preserves equivalent workspace state

title: Workspace panels reference content through stable IDs
examples: panel id 'knowledge-graph' + contentType 'knowledge-graph' instead of embedding component instance
anti_patterns: persisting component closures inside workspace model
tests: registered panel IDs remain deterministic across save/restore

title: Visual tests scope semantic selectors when repeated labels are valid
examples: scope DEMO / MOCK assertion to the intended header or use an explicit first/region locator
anti_patterns: global strict text locator when the UI intentionally repeats the same status label
tests: Playwright selectors remain unambiguous after adding another legitimate status badge

title: Stream semantic class is independent from arrival order
examples: an older primary task remains above a newer background indexing event
anti_patterns: render newest event as most important by default
tests: background event cannot outrank primary solely by timestamp

title: Attention budget caps simultaneous high-prominence information
examples: one primary plus bounded alerts while background work stays collapsed
anti_patterns: all streams request full visual attention
tests: selection honors configured maximums per semantic class

title: Only qualifying alerts may interrupt the current primary task
examples: critical security alert may interrupt; background sync may not
anti_patterns: agent completion toast steals focus from active user task
tests: interrupt decision is deterministic from class, urgency and acknowledgement state

title: Cost of missing influences attention inside a semantic class
examples: two alerts with equal urgency are ordered by cost-of-missing
anti_patterns: confidence or recency alone decides interruption
tests: higher cost-of-missing wins when class/urgency are equal

title: Agent activity is a distinct information stream, not the user task
examples: Makar build completion appears as agent activity unless promoted by an explicit alert
anti_patterns: agent logs replace the user's active task surface
tests: agent stream does not outrank primary without explicit promotion

title: Typed fixtures separate required identity fields from optional overrides
examples: destructure id/class/title, then spread only the remaining override fields
anti_patterns: explicitly assign required properties and then spread an object that may contain them again
tests: TypeScript typecheck reports no TS2783 duplicate-property diagnostics

title: Visualization intent is independent from renderer choice
examples: compare/records may recommend chart while preserving table fallback
anti_patterns: choosing 3D or graph renderer before identifying the information intent
tests: recommendation is deterministic from semantic request without importing renderer library

title: Non-tabular visualizations preserve an accessible fallback
examples: chart has textual/table representation for exact values
anti_patterns: visual-only meaning with no alternative representation
tests: accessible fallback remains available when primary representation changes

title: Avatar identity and behavioral state are independent from renderer
examples: ALINA keeps task and attention while switching hologram to voice-only
anti_patterns: conversation/task state stored inside Three.js scene objects
tests: identity, task and attention survive presentation-mode switch

title: Avatar presentation degrades through explicit renderer capability negotiation
examples: hologram request falls back to portrait on accessible 2D renderer
anti_patterns: failing the avatar entirely when WebGL or motion is unavailable
tests: unsupported mode selects deterministic fallback while preserving persona state

title: Top-level UI changes require explicit test impact review
examples: renaming lab identity requires checking render and Playwright assertions
anti_patterns: change visible product identity while leaving exact-copy tests untouched
tests: context package lists affected UI tests when top-level copy or surface identity changes

title: Composition combines engine contracts without merging their responsibilities
examples: Composition selects graph + compact avatar without embedding stream ranking or avatar state machine
anti_patterns: single god component owns layout, attention, visualization and avatar behavior
tests: composition package depends on engine contracts but engines do not depend on composition

title: Automatic composition decisions require a reason trace
examples: avatar:performance-core:hologram->compact
anti_patterns: layout changes with no inspectable reason
tests: plan exposes deterministic reason strings for scenario and downgrade decisions

title: Human composition overrides are explicit and locked
examples: user locks Context as primary and center region
anti_patterns: automatic recomposition silently moves a user-locked panel
tests: override changes plan and marks affected item locked

title: Scene assets use stable IDs instead of scattered file paths
examples: avatar state references asset:alina:portrait:v1 rather than a component-local /assets path
anti_patterns: renderer/component hard-codes asset path and owns provenance
tests: renderer adapter can switch asset implementation while stable asset ID remains unchanged

title: Cinematic scene features require an operational Core fallback
examples: 3D avatar request degrades to portrait or voice-only without WebGL
anti_patterns: feature disappears or breaks when WebGL is unavailable
tests: Core tier preserves task completion and avatar communication

title: Cinematic features require explicit performance and visual evidence
examples: avatar cinematic mode carries reduced-motion, frame-time and fallback evidence
anti_patterns: calling a feature cinematic based only on a developer-machine screenshot
tests: CI captures quality-budget and visual evidence for cinematic feature changes

title: Graph semantics remain independent from visual renderer
examples: GraphDocument survives DOM/SVG/Canvas/WebGL renderer replacement
anti_patterns: business relation type inferred from line color or renderer object
tests: graph-model imports no renderer package and list fallback preserves relation meaning

title: Renderer capabilities are runtime facts and may be advertised only after successful initialization
examples: 3d capability becomes true only after the WebGL controller is created
anti_patterns: assuming 3d support from requested performance tier alone
tests: capability trace matches actual adapter initialization and falls back on failure

title: Scene renderers own explicit start/stop/resize/dispose lifecycle
examples: cancel animation frame and delete WebGL buffer/program on dispose
anti_patterns: renderer survives product mode change and leaks GPU/browser resources
tests: tier change disposes cinematic ownership and Core reports no 3d

title: Lock one visual MASTER before multiplying screens
examples: one approved 1440px master establishes composition, hierarchy, lighting and component language
anti_patterns: building multiple inconsistent screens before the visual source of truth is accepted
tests: important screen implementation references an approved MASTER baseline

title: Cinematic concepts are decomposed into independent runtime layers
examples: background, environment, hero, real UI, glow, particles and interaction feedback remain separate
anti_patterns: single raster screenshot contains hero, text, buttons and data
tests: removing the hero/background asset leaves the UI structurally usable

title: Character identity is independent from seasonal environment
examples: same canonical heroine can move from winter studio to summer ocean without changing page layout
anti_patterns: layout geometry depends on one exact hero render
tests: season asset swap does not require component-tree rewrite

title: Product icons form one normalized visual language
examples: book, podcast, avatar and image icons share optical size, stroke, padding and glow behavior
anti_patterns: mixing unrelated icon packs and emoji without normalization
tests: icon family passes geometry, stroke and state consistency review

title: Rare high-value motion is preferred over constant decorative motion
examples: eye shimmer pulses irregularly; CTA trail loops slowly; hover glow is brief
anti_patterns: every card, icon and background element animates continuously at high intensity
tests: decorative motion never outranks the primary task and reduced-motion remains usable

title: Seasonal visual change is data-driven, not a duplicate site
examples: monthly theme swaps hero asset, environment, palette, outfit and decor while structure stays stable
anti_patterns: twelve independent pages with copied layout and hard-coded seasonal colors
tests: switching month changes theme payload without structural component changes

title: Pixel-close claims require visual evidence against the approved reference
examples: store reference, implementation screenshot, viewport, commit and known deviations
anti_patterns: declaring visual parity from memory or subjective impression
tests: visual review can trace implementation screenshot to MASTER and commit

title: Performance is part of visual excellence
examples: responsive AVIF/WebP, transform/opacity motion, bounded blur, explicit renderer lifecycle
anti_patterns: cinematic effect accepted despite jank, oversized assets or GPU leaks
tests: cinematic screen meets declared load/frame-time/fallback budget

title: Design every important screen for desktop, tablet and phone from the start
examples: canonical visual baselines: desktop 1440 px, tablet 834 px, phone 390 px
anti_patterns: finish desktop first and postpone tablet/mobile adaptation until the end
scale the desktop canvas proportionally without recomposition
tests: important screen has visual QA screenshots at 1440, 834 and 390 px
primary action remains visible and usable at all three canonical sizes

title: Figma is the visual source of truth; frontend is the executable source of truth
examples: MASTER, tokens, states, responsive layouts and motion intent are defined in Figma before implementation
anti_patterns: frontend invents major visual decisions because the design handoff is incomplete
tests: developer can implement the screen without guessing hierarchy, states or responsive behavior

title: Figma handoff includes MASTER, three responsive layouts, components, asset map and motion spec
examples: desktop 1440, tablet 834, phone 390 plus hover/focus/loading states and asset ownership
anti_patterns: handoff consists only of one desktop screenshot
tests: handoff checklist passes before static implementation starts

title: Commercial Makar sells scoped outcomes, not unbounded frontend hours
examples: Cinematic Landing, Interactive Product Frontend, Cinematic AI Studio packages
anti_patterns: accept vague make-it-beautiful work with no deliverables or acceptance gate
tests: commercial task has deliverables, exclusions, breakpoints, motion tier and acceptance criteria

title: Separate reusable factory IP from client-specific overlays
examples: shared motion/tokens/QA engines plus project brand, hero and business logic overlay
anti_patterns: fork the entire factory for each client
tests: project-specific package can be removed without breaking shared factory packages

title: Commercial production starts only after scope gate
examples: deliverables, 3 breakpoints, motion tier, integrations, asset ownership and review rounds are agreed
anti_patterns: implementation begins from an ambiguous client request
tests: scope gate checklist exists before production branch begins

title: Commercial assets require traceable provenance and usage rights
examples: record source, creator/generator, license, stable asset ID and optimized derivatives
anti_patterns: ship unknown-license font, stock image or icon pack
tests: commercial release manifest has provenance for every non-code asset

title: Acceptance evidence is also portfolio and sales evidence
examples: MASTER + 1440/834/390 screenshots + performance + real integration list + commit
anti_patterns: project finishes with no reproducible proof of quality
tests: release creates an evidence package suitable for acceptance and portfolio redaction

title: Every paid-style project must strengthen the reusable factory
examples: project lesson becomes a reusable package, test, template or knowledge item
anti_patterns: same engineering problem is solved from zero in the next project
tests: post-project review identifies reusable promotions and repeated-work telemetry

title: Books enter Makar KB only through executable patterns and evidence
examples: book chapter becomes principle, pattern, recipe, test, exercise and evidence
anti_patterns: store PDFs or summaries and treat them as learned capability
tests: promoted knowledge item has source, task mapping and validation path

title: Professional learning is staged in waves tied to current product work
examples: Wave 1 targets BOOK-CRAFT composition, design systems, motion, performance and commercial delivery
anti_patterns: ingest an entire library without current-task prioritization
tests: active learning pack maps each source to a current or near-term task

title: Reading does not increase skill maturity without applied evidence
examples: motion principle applied to BOOK-CRAFT and verified through visual QA before skill evidence is updated
anti_patterns: promote K-level because a document was read or summarized
tests: skill promotion references implementation, test, review, benchmark or accepted artifact
